excerpt: Neoway is a Brazilian data and analytics company owned by B3, the Brazilian stock exchange, since 2021. What it does and alternatives.
content:
Neoway is a data and analytics company from Florianópolis, Brazil. Its website, in Portuguese, calls it the largest data and analytics company in Brazil and says it helps businesses become more efficient and cut costs using data analytics and artificial intelligence. In practice it gathers and links large amounts of public and private data about Brazilian companies and people, and sells products built on it for credit decisions, marketing and sales prospecting, fraud prevention and compliance. Customer logos on its site include Banco Inter, BTG Pactual, Hapvida, General Mills, Creditas and Zenvia.

Startupi reported that Neoway was founded in 2002 by Jaime de Paula and moved into big data in 2012. In October 2021 B3, the company that runs Brazil's stock exchange, agreed to buy Neoway for R$1.8 billion, which Latin Lawyer reported as about US$325 million, and set aside up to R$200 million over five years to invest in its growth. At the time Neoway had about 450 employees and more than 500 business customers. B3 said it wanted to build Brazil's largest data hub and expand products in credit, retail, compliance and capital markets. The deal needed approval from CADE, the competition authority, and CVM, the securities regulator; B3 announced that it had been approved, and Gunderson Dettmer, which advised Neoway, dates the completed acquisition to 24 December 2021. Neoway now describes itself as 'uma empresa B3' (a B3 company) and runs as a separately managed business.

Neoway does not publish prices. It sells to companies, mostly large Brazilian firms, through its sales team.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
